env GO111MODULE=off

# Integration test for cache directory calculation (cmd/go/internal/cache).

# go env GOCACHE comes from os.UserCacheDir, which reads XDG_CACHE_HOME and
# then HOME on every host, so this runs everywhere.

mkdir $WORK/gocache
mkdir $WORK/xdg
mkdir $WORK/home

# Set GOCACHE, XDG_CACHE_HOME, and HOME.
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env XDG_CACHE_HOME=$WORK/xdg
env HOME=$WORK/home

# With all three set, we should prefer GOCACHE.
go env GOCACHE
stdout $WORK'/gocache$'

<<<<<<< HEAD
# Without GOCACHE, we should prefer XDG_CACHE_HOME over HOME.
# UserCacheDir joins the path, so the separator is the host's own.
env GOCACHE=
go env GOCACHE
stdout $WORK${/}xdg${/}'go-build$'
=======
# Without GOCACHE, we should prefer XDG_CACHE_HOME over HOME. This answer is
# built rather than echoed, so it carries the host's own separator.
env GOCACHE=
go env GOCACHE
stdout $WORK'[\\/]xdg[\\/]go-build$'
>>>>>>> origin/master

# With only HOME set, we should use $HOME/.cache.
env XDG_CACHE_HOME=
go env GOCACHE
<<<<<<< HEAD
stdout $WORK${/}home${/}'\.cache'${/}'go-build$'
=======
stdout $WORK'[\\/]home[\\/]\.cache[\\/]go-build$'
>>>>>>> origin/master

# With no guidance from the environment, we must disable the cache, but that
# should not cause commands that do not write to the cache to fail. The two
# fallbacks a host can offer for HOME go with it.
env HOME=
env USERPROFILE=
env home=
go env GOCACHE
stdout 'off'
